summary.headline: Supreme Petrochem Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose to Rs 1,957 crore (vs Rs 1,100 crore) with EBITDA Rs 160 crore and PAT near Rs 95 crore, mostly price-driven.
summary.overview: Standalone operating income for Q2 FY27 was Rs 1,957 crore against Rs 1,100 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of Rs 160 crore (8.12% margin) and PAT of about Rs 95 crore, nearly double. Management attributed the revenue jump partly to volumes and mostly to higher selling prices following raw material inflation. H1 FY27 operating income was Rs 3,649 crore, EBITDA Rs 508 crore and PAT Rs 331 crore (9.08% PAT margin), while H1 sales volume fell 3% YoY to 166,085 MT on weaker exports. The company remains debt-free with an investable surplus of Rs 886 crore and approved an interim dividend of Rs 2.5 per share (125%).

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 1,100 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Compounding (PS and ABS)
segments.commentary: Compounding drove the H1 volume growth; internal transfers of PS and ABS to the XPS insulation board division were about 11,700 MT in H1 FY27 vs 4,300 MT a year earlier. Compounding capacity expands from 50,000 to 80,000 TPA, with the step-up targeted around Q3 FY28.

segments.name: XPS insulation board
segments.commentary: Sales are seasonally low in monsoon months. A new wide-width line of 150,000 cubic metres is expected to start commercial production in Q1 FY28, with full absorption over 24 to 30 months.

segments.name: ABS
segments.commentary: Running at about 85% of the truncated 65% rated capacity because of an equipment failure not yet fully repaired. A second ABS line is targeted for Q3 FY29 and is the most capital-intensive project.

segments.name: Polystyrene (EPS/GPPS/HIPS)
segments.commentary: EPS capacity is 145,000 TPA across two locations; India EPS demand is seen at 165,000-170,000 tons this year, with market share below 70%. Specialty share of mix is about 40%. Company market share in polystyrene is about 60%.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Trading sales were about 22% of Q2 sales.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth in FY27-28 is expected to beat last year if US midterm elections clear the war-related disruption; management hopes for improvement from December onwards.
Spreads for GPPS and HIPS in Q2 were about $200-250/t after freight, with HIPS at $300-350/t; spreads are volatile due to freight and raw material costs.
Expected Indian polystyrene demand around 375,000 tons in FY27-28; ABS sales of about 40,000 tons for the full year were floated by an analyst and not disputed.
Management says raw material cost increases are passed through to customers, with a time lag.
Management gave no definitive EBITDA trajectory and cited difficulty forecasting.
capex_capacity: New wide-width XPS insulation board line of 150,000 cubic metres, commercial production from Q1 FY28.
Compounding expansion from 50,000 to 80,000 TPA, targeted around Q3 FY28.
Second ABS line targeted for Q3 FY29; full utilisation of the combined ABS capacity (about 140,000 tons) expected in FY29-30.
ABS plant running at about 85% of truncated 65% rated capacity; equipment repair still incomplete.
Capex is funded entirely from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: Domestic demand in October 2026 described as good, partly attributed to festive season.
Styrene monomer landed price crossed $1,600/t; raw material prices have risen from $900-950 to about $1,650/t.
Duty-free imports of PS and ABS (May-July) pressured domestic prices; imports fell back in August, marginally below last year.
OEM and non-OEM volumes are roughly 50:50; non-OEM demand returned in Q2 after weakness in Q1.
Exports remain hard to execute: ocean freight rose sharply between order and shipment, and the company is not pursuing regular export business at present.
End-market mix is about 40% consumer durables, 30% packaging and 30% stationery; the company has entered auto components and is targeting two-wheeler EV batteries.
Market competition: no European plant closures confirmed by management; new Chinese and ASEAN import pressure noted.

qa_highlights.question: How will styrene pricing and raw material procurement evolve, and will non-OEM players absorb higher prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Landed styrene monomer crossed $1,600/t; the company expects non-OEM pressure if they cannot pass costs on. Domestic raw material requirements are fully met, and improvement is expected from December if geopolitical issues settle.

qa_highlights.question: Is there inventory loss from falling styrene prices in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: No separate inventory loss is booked; SAP uses moving-average valuation, and the market-versus-import price gap is treated as part of normal volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PE and ABS internal transfers to the XPS division rise so sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth came from compounding of PS and ABS. Internal transfers of about 11,700 MT in H1 FY27 versus 4,300 MT last year lifted utilisation, and total volumes exceeded last year, though net market sales fell 2.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise about 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly raw material, including in-transit and high-seas stock on CIF terms, as raw material prices nearly doubled YoY; this stock is expected to be consumed in the following month.

qa_highlights.question: What are the GPPS and HIPS spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads were about $200-250/t for GPPS and about $300-350/t for HIPS after freight and other costs; the spread has narrowed as freight rates rose.

qa_highlights.question: What is the company's market share and India demand outlook for polystyrene?
qa_highlights.answer: India PS demand is about 375,000 tons for FY27-28 per the analyst; the company holds about 60% market share. EPS demand is 165,000-170,000 tons this year, with share below 70%.

risks_watch: Raw material supply from the Gulf and styrene price volatility, with further increases reported in October.
Export recovery is uncertain given freight volatility and order-to-shipment gaps.
ABS equipment repair timeline is unclear; output remains at about 85% of truncated capacity.
Duty-free import waves could return, and competing ABS capacity is in the pipeline.
Non-OEM demand and margin pass-through could weaken if raw material costs keep rising.
Q3 FY28 compounding and Q1 FY28 XPS commissioning timelines need to be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the balance sheet and demand, cautious on the outlook: management repeatedly declined to forecast EBITDA or styrene prices, citing geopolitical and freight volatility, and said exports are difficult at present.
key_quotes: Jump in turnover is partly due to increase in volumes and the balance is all due to increase in the selling prices, consequent to increase in the raw material prices.
Company continues to remain debt-free with an investable surplus of Rs.886 crores as of September 2026.
Now, as far as the margins are concerned, these are all passed through. There could be a lag, time lag for passing on, but it is all passed on.
